To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the compound-extinction procedure was more effective than the simple-extinction procedure in the elimination of fear to a visual stimulus of low associative strength.
compound extinction procedures retard reacquisition to stimuli of low associational strength and facilitate reacquisition to high associational strength.

compound extinction procedures are effective in reducing the reacquisition of conditioned fear, and that the degree of reduction in reacquisition is a function of the associative strengths of stimuli extinguished in combination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a more effective fear-elimination procedure based on the theoretical and empirical findings of Rescorla and Wagner (1972).
the theoretical and practical implications of the Rescorra-Wagner learning theory for fear-elimination therapy.
the development of an animal model for the investigation of the effects of different extinction techniques upon the reacquisition of the conditioned emotional response (CER) in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
compound extinction is more effective than simple extinction in reducing the reacquisition of conditioned fear.
compound extinction procedures appear to be more effective in reducing fear than simple extinction procedures.
compound extinction is a more effective procedure for the elimination of conditioned emotional responses than is simple extinction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
compound extinction procedures are superior to simple procedures when the goal is to reduce the associative strength of stimuli of low associative strengths.
the compound-extinction procedure was more efficacious than the simple-extinction procedure in the elimination of fear to stimuli that had been previously conditioned to elicit fear.
compound-extinction is a more efficacious method for eliminating conditioned fear than simple-extinction, especially when the stimuli to be extinguished are of different associative strengths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Rescorla Wagner model can be used to explain the reacquisition of conditioned fear after compound extinction.
the reacquisition of CRs is dependent on the associative strength of the CSs.

the reacquisition of conditioned fear to stimuli of different associative strengths is retarded when the stimuli are extinguished in compound, and that the degree of “facilitative” or “retardative” effects of compound extinction on fear reacquisition is a function of the difference between the strengths of the stimuli extinguished in the compound.
